title: RSI: overbought isn’t a sell signal
desc: RSI measures speed, and strong trends can stay overbought

cards.title: “Overbought. Sell!”
cards.situation: A stock has climbed for weeks. Its RSI reads 75, above 70. Your friend says: “Overbought. Sell!” Is he right?

chart.label: Price climbs for weeks while RSI stays above 70, now 75

options.text: Yes: above 70 means it will fall
options.feedback: RSI above 70 says price rose fast, not that it must fall. In strong uptrends it can stay up there for weeks.

options.text: Not necessarily: strong trends stay overbought
options.feedback: Overbought means fast, not finished. Strong trends can stay above 70 for a long time.
Above 70 isn’t a buy signal either. RSI only says price rose fast; it doesn’t say what comes next.

cards.work: RSI crossed 70 weeks ago. Since then, price rose about another 24%.

cards.title: RSI: a speed gauge
cards.text: The **[[rsi|Relative Strength Index]]** compares the size of recent up days with recent down days, usually over 14 days. It always reads between 0 and 100.

visual.label: RSI scale: below 30 oversold, 30 to 70 neutral, above 70 overbought

blocks.tip: Fast isn’t the same as finished. RSI measures speed, not value.

cards.title: Strong trends stay overbought
cards.text: Watch RSI cross 70, then stay there while price keeps climbing.

chart.label: RSI crosses 70, then stays there while price rises another 24%

cards.foot: Selling the first time RSI hit 70 meant missing the next 24%. Here, [[overbought|overbought]] was a sign of strength.

cards.title: Let the trend lead
cards.text: In an uptrend, RSI often swings between **40 and 80**. Watch the dips toward 40, not the peaks above 70. The classic 70 and 30 work best when the market goes sideways.

cards.title: Read the gauge
cards.q: A stock’s RSI reads 25. What does that tell you?

visual.label: RSI marker at 25, inside the oversold band

options.feedback: Below 30 means price fell fast lately. That’s all it says: it can keep falling.

options.text: The stock is cheap: buy now
options.feedback: Below 30 just means price dropped fast. It can keep falling, so oversold isn’t a buy signal on its own.
RSI reads only price changes. It says nothing about the business: just that price fell fast.
RSI is built from price changes, not volume. A reading of 25 means price fell fast.

cards.title: Where 70 and 30 work
cards.q: When do the 70 and 30 lines work best as turning points?

options.feedback: In a strong uptrend RSI can stay above 70 for weeks. In a range, price swings between floor and ceiling, so the extremes turn more often.
In a range, price swings between floor and ceiling, so readings near 70 and 30 turn more often.
In a strong downtrend RSI can stay below 30 for weeks. The extremes turn most often in a range.
They do work, just not everywhere. In a sideways range, the extremes turn more often.

cards.headline: You can read RSI without panicking.
lines: RSI runs 0 to 100 and measures speed.
Above 70 is overbought, below 30 oversold: fast, not finished.
Strong trends stay overbought. Let the trend lead.
